extracted.intended_audience: colleges, universities, and other Title IX recipient institutions and their Title IX personnel (Coordinators, investigators, decision-makers, and informal resolution facilitators)
extracted.subtask_short: Title IX training and grievance rules
extracted.subtask_description: Explanatory preamble to final Title IX regulations specifying required training topics, procedural protections (including presumption of non-responsibility), posting/transparency obligations, and limits on permissible training content for personnel who carry out Title IX grievance processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training on the definition of sexual harassment (§106.30)
rubrics_metrics.description: The training on the definition of sexual harassment in this provision was intended to refer to the definition of sexual harassment in §106.30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 106.45(b)(1)(iii) was revised to clarify that training on the definition of sexual harassment means the definition in §106.30.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory training to promote Title IX purpose and compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandatory training for Title IX personnel that promotes the purpose of a Title IX process and compliance with these final regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision prescribes mandatory training while leaving recipients free to adopt additional education and training content that they believe serves their community's needs; the Department does not view this as removing other vital training regarding responses to sexual harassment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing: train personnel when serving in role (no specified frequency)
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulation requires that any Title IX Coordinator, investigator, decision-maker, or person who facilitates an informal resolution process will, when serving in such a role, be trained to serve in that role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulations do not impose an annual or other frequency condition; recipients have flexibility to determine the extent and timing of additional training so they can allocate resources among Title IX obligations and other institutional needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-maker training on conducting grievance processes and using hearing technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision-makers must receive training in how to conduct a grievance process including how to use technology that will be used by a recipient to conduct a live hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department revised §106.45(b)(1)(iii) to emphasize training on hearings and technology used at live hearings so decision-makers can conduct the grievance process effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigators and decision-makers trained on issues of relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators and decision-makers must be trained on issues of the relevance of questions and evidence (including how to determine the relevance or irrelevance of a complainant's prior sexual history).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators should receive training on relevance so they can prepare investigative reports that fairly summarize relevant evidence; decision-makers must be trained on relevance to evaluate questions and evidence during hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training materials must not rely on sex stereotypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Training materials 'must' not rely on sex stereotypes (changed from 'may' to 'must').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declined to catalog specific notions that constitute sex stereotypes and instead adopted a broad prohibition so decisions are based on individualized facts, not stereotypical notions about what 'men' or 'women' do. This does not prevent referencing evidence-based research, provided it is not relied on to apply generalizations to particular allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research may be referenced but not relied upon to generalize to particular cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Training content can reference evidence-based information or peer-reviewed scientific research into sexual violence dynamics, including the impact of trauma, but cannot be relied on to apply generalizations to particular allegations of sexual harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A fact-specific evaluation of training materials and their use is needed to determine compliance with §106.45(b)(1)(iii). Use of research is permitted where it does not 'rely' on sex stereotypes or apply group generalizations to individual cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting training materials for transparency (§106.45(b)(10))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are required to post on the recipient's website the training materials referred to in §106.45(b)(1)(iii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This transparency allows the recipient's community and the public to view the approach to training and hold the recipient accountable for compliance with the final regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parameters apply only to materials used to carry out Title IX obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department places reasonable conditions on materials specifically used by recipients to carry out obligations under these regulations without interfering with curricular or academic instruction control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department is not proactively scouring curricula for sex stereotyping; requirements apply to training materials used for compliance with these regulations and recipients retain discretion over curricula.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility to include additional training topics (not mandated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients have discretion to choose additional training topics (e.g., neurobiology of trauma, assessing credibility in trauma, Clery/FERPA intersections, affirmative consent, cultural competency), but the Department declines to mandate these topics in the final regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule strikes a balance between mandating necessary topics and allowing flexibility so institutions can design training appropriate to their community; the Department declined to expand mandatory topics suggested by commenters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of persons facilitating informal resolution processes
rubrics_metrics.description: The list of Title IX personnel who must receive the specified training was revised to add 'any person who facilitates an informal resolution process' in addition to Title IX Coordinators, investigators, and decision-makers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change responds to concerns that informal processes could involve untrained personnel; training and conflict-of-interest protections must apply to informal resolution facilitators as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training must cover the scope of the recipient's education program or activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Training requirements were revised to require training on the 'scope of the recipient's education program or activity' so recipients correctly treat incidents within that scope as Title IX matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps ensure recipients do not inadvertently exclude incidents (for example, off-campus conduct) that are within the recipient's education program or activity from Title IX consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training must include appeals and informal resolution processes (as applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Add training on appeals and informal resolution processes in addition to hearings (as applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The revisions specify that Title IX personnel must be trained on the procedures and roles involved in appeals and in facilitating informal resolution, where those processes are used by the recipient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department may review training materials regardless of recipient designation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department reserves the right to examine training materials whether or not a recipient has specifically designated the material as essential to performing a Title IX role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows reasonable gauging of compliance and prevents institutions from avoiding scrutiny by not labeling materials as 'essential.'

rubrics_metrics.name: No mandated mentor requirement or mandatory trainer qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to require that Title IX personnel be 'mentored' before working with parties or to prescribe qualifications for training presenters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance is enforced based on whether a recipient trains Title IX personnel in conformity with §106.45(b)(1)(iii), not on trainer credentials; recipients are encouraged to use qualified, experienced professionals but the Department does not certify or endorse providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of trauma-informed practices in training
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department allows recipients flexibility regarding trauma-informed practices but mandates that training materials avoid prejudgment and bias; there is no fixed definition of 'trauma-informed' across contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters offered conflicting views; the Department notes that trauma-informed practices may be possible to apply impartially but are challenging. The final rule forbids bias/conflicts of interest and precludes materials relying on sex stereotypes; recipients may adopt trauma-informed elements as long as they remain consistent with impartiality and other legal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free-from-conflict/bias requirement for Title IX personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must ensure Title IX personnel are free from conflicts of interest and bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement applies to Title IX Coordinators, investigators, decision-makers, and persons who facilitate informal resolution processes; training must include how to avoid bias and conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of non-responsibility until conclusion of grievance process
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's grievance process must apply a presumption that a respondent is not responsible until conclusion of a grievance process (the 'presumption').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presumption is intended to ensure decisions are based on evidence rather than assumptions, to reinforce correct application of the chosen evidentiary standard, and to prevent treating respondents as responsible prior to an outcome. The presumption must be included in initial written notice to both parties after a formal complaint is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof on the recipient (not parties)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations place the burden of proof solely on the recipient, not on a complainant or respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presumption helps protect the correct application of the burden and evidentiary standard and is consistent with ensuring impartial proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption does not limit supportive measures for complainants
rubrics_metrics.description: The presumption of non-responsibility does not interfere with a complainant's right to receive supportive measures with or without filing a formal complaint under §106.44(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must respond promptly to actual knowledge of sexual harassment and offer supportive measures designed to restore or preserve equal educational access regardless of the presumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on prejudgment and status-based credibility determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX personnel must interact with both complainant and respondent impartially throughout the grievance process without prejudgment of the facts at issue and without drawing inferences about credibility based on a party's status as a complainant or respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulations preclude credibility determinations or other inferences that rest solely on a party's status; credibility and responsibility conclusions must be based on objective evaluation of relevant evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charging materially false statements is not automatically retaliation
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.71(b)(2) clarifies that charging an individual with a code of conduct violation for making a materially false statement in bad faith in the course of a grievance process does not constitute retaliation, but a determination regarding responsibility alone is not sufficient to conclude that an individual made a materially false statement in bad faith.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must be careful to base any finding of materially false statements on a separate determination of bad faith, not solely on the outcome of the grievance process.
